items.followUp: How does the value of g change as altitude above Earth’s surface increases?

rubric.why: Award for identifying a cause of the variation of g with latitude.
rubric.how: State that Earth’s non-spherical shape or rotation causes g to vary from place to place.

rubric.why: Award for stating how g changes with altitude.
rubric.how: State that g decreases as altitude increases.

modelAnswer: The value of g varies with place because Earth is not a perfect sphere and because of Earth’s rotation; g is greater at the poles than at the equator.
The value of g also decreases with increasing altitude above Earth’s surface.

items.followUp: State two environmental disadvantages of burning fossil fuels.

rubric.why: Award for identifying that fossil fuels are a finite resource.
rubric.how: State that fossil fuels are non-renewable, limited in supply, or will eventually run out.

rubric.why: Award for naming an environmental harm caused by using fossil fuels.
rubric.how: Name pollution or global warming as a disadvantage.

modelAnswer: Fossil fuels are non-renewable, so their supplies are limited and will eventually run out.
Burning them causes pollution, including greenhouse-gas emissions that contribute to global warming.

items.followUp: Define gravitational potential energy and write its equation near Earth’s surface.

rubric.why: Award for defining kinetic energy in terms of motion.
rubric.how: State that kinetic energy is the energy a body possesses because of its motion.

rubric.why: Award for the correct kinetic-energy equation.

modelAnswer: Kinetic energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its motion.
K.E. = ½mv², where m is the mass of the body and v is its speed.

items.followUp: Define efficiency and write its formula as a percentage.

rubric.why: Award for defining efficiency as a comparison of useful output with total input.
rubric.how: State that efficiency is the ratio of useful output to total input.

rubric.why: Award for stating the percentage formula for efficiency.

modelAnswer: Efficiency is the ratio of useful output to total input.

items.followUp: Define density and write its formula.

rubric.why: Award for defining pressure in terms of force and area.
rubric.how: State that pressure is the force acting per unit area.

rubric.why: Award for the correct pressure formula.

modelAnswer: Pressure is the force acting per unit area.
P = F/A, where F is force and A is area.
